title: Rust-first routing and rendering cleanup
description: Address user-reported architecture drift by making Rust the source of truth for request routing, date/time computation, formatting, and HTML rendering while shrinking Worker JS to host-adapter responsibilities only.

title: Switch Rust router to tuple match and full route set
description: Replace imperative route checks with tuple-pattern routing and include all app routes needed by runtime dispatch, including theme and static passthrough identifiers.

title: Collapse Worker to single Rust route dispatch
description: Remove ad-hoc per-path JS branching and dispatch all non-host responsibilities from a single Rust route_id decision path.

title: Adopt chrono for Rust time generation and formatting
description: Move clock time derivation/formatting into Rust using chrono (with wasm support) so JS no longer computes HH/MM/SS.

title: Adopt Rust templating crate for home rendering
description: Replace manual string replacement templating with a crate-based renderer for HTML payload generation and clearer field binding semantics.

title: Document and justify remaining JS blocks
description: For each remaining JS block, document why it must stay in JS (host/runtime boundary, browser-only timezone hinting, or asset adapter) and remove anything unjustified.

description: Update build script to generate JS/WASM bindings in rust/clock-wasm/pkg via wasm-bindgen CLI.

title: Add typed Rust exports for route/context/render
description: Expose wasm-bindgen-friendly APIs for route id, request context resolution, and rendering outputs with behavior parity.

title: Phase 2: Cut Worker to typed bindings
description: Refactor Worker to consume typed bindings and remove low-level pointer marshalling/read helpers.

title: Replace pointer ABI calls in worker
description: Use wasm-bindgen generated module init and typed function calls for context and rendering flows.

title: Keep host-only logic in worker
description: Retain SSE lifecycle, ASSETS adapter, and Response construction while preserving behavior.

title: Phase 3: Remove legacy ABI and verify parity
description: Delete obsolete pointer ABI surface and update tests/checks/docs to final architecture.

title: Remove obsolete Rust/Worker ABI glue
description: Delete no-longer-used legacy pointer exports/helpers and simplify code paths.

title: Update docs and run full quality gates
description: Refresh README/live checks for typed ABI and pass build, rust tests, live checks, and full test pipeline.

title: Worker collapse phase 3: Rust-owned request context
description: Eliminate remaining repetitive Worker request preprocessing by moving all transferable timezone/theme/query/cookie normalization and precedence logic into Rust while preserving only host-runtime responsibilities in JS.

title: Build Rust request-context resolver ABI
description: Define a single Rust resolver export that accepts request hints (query/header/cookie/theme/hx) and returns resolved timezone/theme values, precedence decisions, and cookie-write directives via stable buffers and status bits.

title: Parse query/cookie inputs in Rust
description: Move tz/theme query parsing and cookie extraction out of Worker JS into Rust helpers, including robust percent-decoding behavior and invalid input handling.

title: Resolve theme/timezone precedence in Rust
description: Apply canonical precedence (tz query > x-timezone header > clock_tz cookie, theme query > clock_theme cookie) and emit explicit cookie-update flags.

title: Collapse Worker preprocessing to one Rust context call
description: Refactor fetch handler to consume one Rust context result and remove JS normalizeTheme/readCookieValue branching and duplicated cookie decision logic.

title: Remove repetitive response cookie branching
description: Centralize response finalization so timezone/theme cookie directives are applied once per response path rather than repeated in each route branch.

title: Prove parity and document irreducible JS
description: Expand Rust unit tests and live endpoint checks for resolver precedence and cookie behavior; update docs with the final minimal JS blocks that cannot move to Rust.

title: Extend live checks for precedence matrix
description: Cover query-vs-header precedence, cookie fallback, unchanged-cookie no-write behavior, malformed cookie entries, and theme precedence HTMX/non-HTMX responses on port 5656.

title: Document final Worker-only responsibilities
description: Record each remaining JS block with explicit host-runtime justification (WASM bridge, Response construction, SSE stream lifecycle, ASSETS fetch adapter).
